summary: Two range lights the Department of Marine built in 1898 to lead ships into South Bay, Manitoulin Island; kept by the Ritchie family, later automated.

notes_for_editor: Keeper rows for 1902, 1906 and 1914 are matched by OCR line (the 1902 list prints the name and station on one line, Ritchie, James South Bay Range Lights; the 1906 and 1914 lists read the same way). Page images were not viewed for these rows. The 1909 and 1910 salary tables are OCR'd as '1.50 00' (1909) and '150 00' (1910, clean); the 1910 figure supports the $150 reading. The 1898 construction facts come only through LighthouseFriends, which quotes the Department's 1898 report; the corpus starts in 1900, so the primary 1898 report has not been checked. The 1898 description gives a fixed white light (front and rear); Rowlett gives a continuous green light today (LighthouseFriends' table gives Fixed Green); no source dates the change. Rear tower: 40 ft (12.2 m) in 1898 against the record's current 10.9 m (LighthouseFriends table); not reconciled. The front tower's 8.5 m in the record is the 1898 height to the vane (28 ft) and the same figure as Rowlett's focal plane; Rowlett's tower height is 5 m (17 ft) and LighthouseFriends' table 8.0 m, so the record's structure height needs a reviewer. Rowlett's 'Visible from the ferry' line belongs to the Cove Island entry, not South Baymouth; the story now cites LighthouseFriends for the ferry view. The 'Site open, tower closed' quote is now the South Baymouth entry's own wording. Leonard Leeson is named only as LighthouseFriends names him (brother-in-law); the 2012 medal buyer, a private collector named by LighthouseFriends, is not named in the story. No storms, wrecks or rescues were found in the sources read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1898 report (via LighthouseFriends) puts the front light on the south-east end of a bare limestone island; the Canadian Coast Guard list calls it a small island; the Lighthouse Directory places it on the rocky beach just west of the ferry terminal; LighthouseFriends' visitor notes send visitors down to the rocky beach. The story states the disagreement and does not settle it.
